name: Bowie Knife
description: A large fixed-blade knife with a distinctive clipped point and a crossguard. Originally designed for hunting and self-defense on the American frontier, it became an icon of the Old West.

name: Karambit
description: A small curved blade modeled after a tiger's claw. Designed to be held with the index finger through a ring, allowing a secure grip and slashing motions in close combat.

name: Stiletto
description: A slender, pointed dagger purpose-built for thrusting through gaps in armor. Its narrow blade gives it minimal cutting edge but exceptional piercing ability.

name: Puukko
description: A traditional Finnish belt knife carried as an everyday tool for generations. Simple, sturdy, and elegant — used for everything from food prep to woodcraft.

name: Tanto
description: A Japanese dagger with a thick spine and a distinctively angular chisel point. Carried by samurai as a backup weapon, also used in ritual suicide (seppuku).

name: Sgian-dubh
handle: Carved wood, often with a gem
description: A small Scottish single-edge knife traditionally worn tucked into the top of the kilt hose. Today it's a decorative element of Highland dress, though historically functional.

name: Kukri
description: The iconic inward-curved blade of the Gurkha warriors. The recurve concentrates chopping power and makes it equally effective as a utility tool or weapon.

name: Dirk
description: A long thrusting dagger historically worn by Scottish Highlanders and naval officers. A transitional piece between a dagger and a short sword.

name: Neck Knife
description: A compact fixed-blade knife worn on a cord around the neck, inside the shirt. Designed for concealed carry and fast deployment in emergency situations.

name: Fillet Knife
description: A long, thin, extremely flexible blade designed to slide cleanly along the backbone of a fish. Its flex allows precise cuts while minimizing waste.

name: Athame
description: A ritual double-edged dagger used in Wiccan and Neopagan ceremonies. It is traditionally not used for physical cutting but as a symbolic tool to direct energy.

name: Boot Knife
description: A compact, slim-profiled knife designed to be carried concealed in a boot. Favored by gamblers, outlaws, and later by military personnel as a backup blade.

name: Oyster Knife
description: A short, stiff blade with a blunt tip designed to pry open oyster shells without slipping. The wide handle provides the leverage needed for tough shells.

name: Push Dagger
description: A small dagger with a T-shaped handle gripped in the fist so the blade projects between the fingers. Designed for close-range stabbing with the full force of a punch.

name: Ulu
description: A unique fan-shaped blade with the handle mounted above the center of the blade. Used for thousands of years by Inuit peoples for butchering animals, scraping hides, and preparing food.

name: Whittling Knife
description: A simple, short-bladed knife optimized for carving wood by hand. The small blade gives precise control when shaping figures, utensils, and craft objects.

name: Folding Karambit
handle: Aluminum or G10 with finger ring
description: A modern EDC interpretation of the traditional karambit with a folding mechanism for safe pocket carry. Retains the hooked blade and retention ring of its ancestor.

name: Misericorde
description: Known as the 'dagger of mercy,' this narrow-bladed weapon was used to deliver a killing blow through the visor or joints of a downed, armored opponent.

name: Hunting Skinner
description: A fixed-blade knife with a gently curved drop-point or integrated gut hook, optimized for field dressing and skinning game without puncturing the stomach cavity.

name: Trench Knife
description: Developed for brutal close-quarters combat in the narrow trenches of WWI. Features a spiked or knuckle-duster handle for use as a bludgeon alongside the blade.

name: Grapefruit Knife
description: A specialized kitchen knife with a long, curved, double-sided serrated blade designed to segment citrus fruits by running along the inside of the rind.

name: Kpinga
description: A uniquely shaped throwing knife with multiple blades at different angles, designed to strike a target regardless of rotational orientation during flight.

name: Cheese Knife
description: A kitchen knife with holes in the blade to prevent cheese from sticking, or a forked tip for serving. Different shapes exist for hard, semi-soft, and soft cheeses.

name: Khukuri Companion Knives
description: Two small knives traditionally stored in the back pockets of a kukri sheath — one blunt (for starting fires with a flint) and one sharp (a small utility knife called a karda).

name: Navaja
description: A traditional Spanish folding knife with a long blade that locks open via a spring or notch. Historically used as a working knife and weapon by Spanish laborers and sailors.
